questions.question: Most respondents in the 2024 St. Lawrence County youth assessment said they had never tried this substance shown in its survey chart.

source.citation: St. Lawrence County Youth Bureau. (2024). 2024 needs assessment summary. St. Lawrence County. https://www.stlawco.gov/sites/default/files/CommunityServices/2026_LSP_St.%20Lawrence.pdf#page=32
source.explanation: The survey chart shows many more respondents saying no than yes to ever trying marijuana. It reports lifetime experience and does not measure caffeine use.

questions.question: According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, avoiding this stimulant is the best choice for children and teens.

source.citation: Corkins, M. (2025, August 11). The effects of caffeine on kids: A parent's guide. HealthyChildren.org. https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/the-effects-of-caffeine-on-kids-a-parents-guide.aspx
source.explanation: The AAP recommends avoiding caffeine for kids. Age 12 is not a threshold that makes caffeinated drinks appropriate.

questions.question: CDC estimates that about 3 in 10 people who use this substance have a use disorder involving that substance.

source.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024, December 5). Understanding your risk for cannabis use disorder. https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/cannabis-use-disorder.html
source.explanation: This is a national CDC estimate about cannabis use disorder, not a St. Lawrence County rate or a 30-day quitting statistic.

questions.question: Coffee and tea are commonly shared at gatherings. Which stimulant do these beverages naturally contain?

source.citation: National Library of Medicine. (2021, September 8). Caffeine. MedlinePlus. https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html
source.explanation: Coffee beans and tea leaves naturally contain caffeine. Caffeine is also added to some drinks and medicines.

questions.question: Someone who regularly drinks coffee suddenly stops. Withdrawal from this substance can cause headache, drowsiness and irritability.

source.citation: National Library of Medicine. (2021, September 8). Caffeine. MedlinePlus. https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html
source.explanation: Regular caffeine use can lead to withdrawal when stopped suddenly. Possible symptoms include headache, drowsiness and irritability.

source.citation: Corkins, M. (2025, August 11). The effects of caffeine on kids: A parent's guide. HealthyChildren.org. https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/the-effects-of-caffeine-on-kids-a-parents-guide.aspx
source.explanation: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system and can increase alertness.

questions.question: This drug contains THC, a compound that can alter perception and cause an intoxicating high.

source.citation: New York State Office of Cannabis Management. (n.d.). Adult-use information. Retrieved November 5, 2026, from https://cannabis.ny.gov/adult-use-information
source.explanation: THC is the cannabis compound known for psychoactive and intoxicating effects, including changes in perception.

questions.question: CDC warns that this substance can slow reaction time and impair coordination, making driving unsafe.

source.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024, February 22). Cannabis and driving. https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/driving.html
source.explanation: Cannabis can slow reactions, impair coordination and distort perception. Those effects make driving dangerous.

questions.question: THC in this substance can interfere with a student's memory, attention and learning.

source.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024, February 15). Cannabis and teens. https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/cannabis-and-teens.html
source.explanation: CDC identifies memory, learning and attention problems among the negative effects of teen cannabis use.

questions.question: CDC lists continuing use despite relationship problems as a warning sign of this substance's use disorder.

source.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024, December 5). Understanding your risk for cannabis use disorder. https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/cannabis-use-disorder.html
source.explanation: Continuing cannabis use despite social or relationship problems is one listed sign of cannabis use disorder.

questions.question: Which statement about out-of-pocket costs for cannabis treatment is accurate?
choices: Every insured person pays the same price
Costs depend on the plan and services
Having insurance removes every treatment cost
All treatment requires the same inpatient program

source.citation: HealthCare.gov. (n.d.). Your total costs for health care: Premium, deductible, and out-of-pocket costs. Retrieved November 5, 2026, from https://www.healthcare.gov/choose-a-plan/your-total-costs/
source.explanation: Deductibles, copayments, coinsurance and covered services affect what a person pays for care. Check the specific plan and services.

questions.question: Regular use of this THC-containing substance during adolescence can harm learning and memory.

source.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. (2024, February 15). Cannabis and teens. https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/cannabis-and-teens.html
source.explanation: Cannabis use during adolescence can affect learning and memory while the brain is developing. The wording describes a risk, not an inevitable outcome for every person.

questions.question: In the 2024 St. Lawrence County youth assessment, about 650 respondents said this substance was very difficult to obtain.

source.citation: St. Lawrence County Youth Bureau. (2024). 2024 needs assessment summary. St. Lawrence County. https://www.stlawco.gov/sites/default/files/CommunityServices/2026_LSP_St.%20Lawrence.pdf#page=32
source.explanation: This is an approximate reading of the marijuana bar in the report, not an exact published count. The survey included 1,767 youth and teens; the chart does not measure caffeine.

questions.question: In the 2024 St. Lawrence County youth assessment, which issue ranked second among concerns about peers?

source.citation: St. Lawrence County Youth Bureau. (2024). 2024 needs assessment summary. St. Lawrence County. https://www.stlawco.gov/sites/default/files/CommunityServices/2026_LSP_St.%20Lawrence.pdf#page=32
source.explanation: The ranking describes what surveyed youth were concerned about. It is not a marijuana-use rate. The assessment included 1,767 youth and participation from 16 of 18 districts.

questions.question: Under New York law, what is the minimum age for adult-use cannabis in St. Lawrence County?

source.citation: New York State Office of Cannabis Management. (n.d.). Adult-use information. Retrieved November 5, 2026, from https://cannabis.ny.gov/adult-use-information
source.explanation: New York's adult-use rule applies across the state, including St. Lawrence County. The medical cannabis program has separate rules.

questions.question: Someone stops using marijuana, then starts using it again. Which health term describes this?
choices: Return to use, sometimes called relapse

source.citation: A.D.A.M., Inc. (n.d.). Substance use - marijuana. In A.D.A.M. medical encyclopedia. MedlinePlus. Retrieved November 5, 2026, from https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000796.htm
source.explanation: Starting to use marijuana again after a period without it is a return to use; relapse is another term for it.

questions.question: Which symptoms can occur when someone stops heavy or long-term marijuana use?
choices: A new cannabis high without taking cannabis
Permanent loss of the need for sleep

source.citation: A.D.A.M., Inc. (n.d.). Substance use - marijuana. In A.D.A.M. medical encyclopedia. MedlinePlus. Retrieved November 5, 2026, from https://medlineplus.gov/ency/patientinstructions/000796.htm
source.explanation: Some people experience anxiety, irritability or sleep difficulties when stopping cannabis. These symptoms are possible, not inevitable.

questions.question: What type of drug is caffeine?

source.citation: Corkins, M. (2025, August 11). The effects of caffeine on kids: A parent's guide. HealthyChildren.org. https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/the-effects-of-caffeine-on-kids-a-parents-guide.aspx
source.explanation: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system and can increase alertness.

questions.question: A regular caffeine user suddenly stops. Which symptom can occur during withdrawal?
choices: A new stimulant high without caffeine
A permanent decrease in the need for sleep

source.citation: National Library of Medicine. (2021, September 8). Caffeine. MedlinePlus. https://medlineplus.gov/caffeine.html
source.explanation: MedlinePlus lists headache, drowsiness, irritability, nausea and difficulty concentrating as possible caffeine withdrawal symptoms.
